ev.q: so that the capsule was driven forward by the difference in pressure

1.why: B段整段讲系统如何运作：载体放进铜管，蒸汽泵压缩或抽走空气，靠压差推动。标题 v “How air pressure was put to work” ↔ 原文 “driven forward by the difference in pressure”。干扰项 ii 提到 first tubes，但B段只提到伦敦第一条线很短，没有讲建造成本。

ev.q: For several decades the system performed remarkably well.

2.why: C段先讲速度（30公里/小时，比街上任何车辆都快），再讲公众热情（petit bleu）和鼎盛期的运量。标题 viii “Speed and popularity at its height” ↔ “performed remarkably well / adopted the service with enthusiasm / At its peak”。

ev.q: Yet the technology had weaknesses that became more serious as networks expanded.

3.why: D段先讲技术问题（卡管、难定位、需挖路），再讲经济问题（运营成本上升而价格固定）。iv “technical and financial difficulties” 同时概括了这两部分。ii 的 cost 指建造成本，而原文说的是 operating costs（运营成本），是典型的同词干扰。

ev.q: The decline of the pneumatic post was gradual rather than sudden.

4.why: E段讲衰落：电话、电传打字机逐步取代了它，各城市陆续关闭。vi “A slow replacement by newer methods” ↔ “gradual rather than sudden” + telephone / teleprinter。

ev.q: Pneumatic tubes did not disappear, however.

5.why: F段前半讲至今仍在医院、银行使用（surviving uses），后半讲 Ribeiro 与 Ellison 对其意义的不同看法（differing interpretations）。

ev.q: since a message only ever needed to pass through one central exchange rather than a chain of intermediate stations

6.why: Keiko Sato 认为巴黎的放射状布局（radial layout）是效率关键：信件只需经过一个中心交换站。题干 “the way the lines were arranged” ↔ “radial layout”，“fewer stages” ↔ “one central exchange rather than a chain of intermediate stations”。

ev.q: its operating costs per message rose steadily after 1900

7.why: Lars Hedberg 研究柏林系统的账目后指出，运营成本持续上升，而公众支付的价格几乎不变。题干 “more expensive to run” ↔ “operating costs … rose”，“income stayed largely the same” ↔ “price … barely changed”。

ev.q: its speed did not depend on traffic or weather

8.why: 这句话出自 Ellison 的说法（According to … Margaret Ellison）。题干 “unaffected by conditions on the roads” ↔ “did not depend on traffic or weather”。

ev.q: a system designed to solve one specific problem could not adapt once that problem had been solved by other means

9.why: Ellison 认为问题不在于技术有缺陷，而在于它被取代了：它要解决的问题已经被别的手段解决。题干 “the need it served was met in other ways” ↔ “that problem had been solved by other means”。Ribeiro 讲的是与现代胶囊列车的物理原理相同，与本题无关。

ev.q: A cylindrical carrier, usually made of leather-covered steel and roughly the size of a rolled newspaper, was placed inside a brass tube.

10.why: 空格前是 “a container known as a”，需要填名词。原文中被放进铜管、由覆皮钢制成的东西是 carrier。“steel with a leather covering” ↔ “leather-covered steel”。

ev.q: Steam-driven pumps at a central station then either compressed the air behind the carrier or removed the air in front of it

11.why: “pumps … powered by ___” ↔ “Steam-driven pumps”，driven 对应 powered by，填 steam。

ev.q: delivered to an address on the other side of the city within two hours

12.why: “in no more than ___” ↔ “within two hours”，“the opposite side of the city” ↔ “the other side of the city”。两个词，没有超出字数限制。

ev.q: Engineers developed an ingenious way of finding stuck carriers by firing a pistol into the tube and timing the echo

13.why: 定位卡住的载体靠的是向管内开枪再听回声。“found it by firing a ___” ↔ “finding stuck carriers by firing a pistol”，“measuring how long the echo took” ↔ “timing the echo”，填 pistol。
